title: #6 - I Surrender
content:
#6 - I Surrender

Chapter 6 I Surrender

Facing Arthur's attack, Roger swung his sword to block.

According to his plan, after this action, he would chop hard and knock Arthur's sword off.

After that, the young lord would kneel on the ground and beg for mercy, and he would kill Arthur after giving Brynden a few comments, and the action would end perfectly.

Wasn't the territory in hand?

It's just that his plan was too ideal.

As we all know, ideals are full and reality is very skinny.

The skinny reality is that Arthur's big sword swung down from the top was so powerful that Roger didn't block it at the first time, and then the sword he held with both hands was slowly pressed down.

How could it be so powerful? Roger was shocked and couldn't believe it.

Arthur's body burst out with a powerful force that was inconsistent with his body size.

At this time, he didn't have the mind to comment.

Fortunately, many years of experience made him make the right choice:

Back off to relieve the force to avoid this attack.

Because Roger pulled away too quickly, sparks even rubbed between the blades of the two swords.

Brynden on the horse opened his eyes wide and looked at the scene in disbelief.

Roger, who was just relaxed and casually pointing out the world, was actually chopped back two steps by a sword.

And Jules, who was about to slip away behind Arthur, had his pupils shrink, and was obviously shocked by his nephew's chop.

He asked himself if he could make the middle-aged bandit with such well-developed arm muscles retreat two steps with just one sword.

Amber also looked at his lord in disbelief. Living together day and night, he knew Arthur's fighting power best.

What happened?

The four Bracken soldiers behind were even more stunned. They never thought that Lord Arthur was so strong.

The next scene shocked them even more.

Arthur swung the sword again and chopped straight at the middle-aged bandit.

Roger had no choice but to block again.

But Arthur, who had already tested his opponent, used 90% of his strength this time, striving to succeed in one strike.

You know, he only used 50% of his strength just now.

The effect of this strike was very obvious, and Roger couldn't block it at all. In order to relieve the force, he had to kneel on one knee.

The palms of his hands holding the sword were numb, and Roger felt that the power transmitted from the sword was not like a person, but a ferocious large beast.

This was the first time he encountered such an opponent in his nearly 20 years of fighting career.

No skills, all strength.

But he could defeat himself with strength alone.

Time may have only passed for a while, but in the eyes of Roger who was struggling to hold on, it was as long as this long summer.

Suddenly, the sword felt lighter, and Roger was relieved for no reason.

But before he could react, Arthur's third sword immediately chopped down.

With a clang, Roger, who was unable to use his strength, had his sword knocked off.

Fortunately, he was smart and retracted his body, so that Arthur's sword, which was still coming, did not hit him.

Immediately, the sword, still buzzing, was placed across Roger's neck.

Roger's head was buzzing, and the cold touch of the sword on his neck made him speechless.

The people around him were all speechless.

Whether it was the soldiers of the Brackens, the soldiers of the Blackwoods disguised as bandits, or Brynden, Jules, and Amber.

No one could have imagined that Arthur, who looked thin, young and inexperienced, would win.

And he won so easily.

The silence in the field could hear the birds chirping nearby.

The young Brynden looked at Arthur holding Roger's neck with a sword in one hand, and was so stunned that he couldn't speak.

In his eyes at this moment, Arthur's previous actions were not because he was an inexperienced newcomer in battle.

But it was because the master disdained to abide by the nonsense rules of low-level warriors.

This is the real master, the future head of the Blackwood family thought secretly in his heart.

Then Arthur's words broke the silence in the beech forest.

"Weren't you quite talkative just now?" Arthur increased the strength of his hand, "Now give me some comments."

Blood gradually seeped out of Roger's neck, he felt his heart pounding, life seemed to be slipping away, and the fear of death had never been so real.

The desire to live made him shout hurriedly: "Don't kill me, I surrender, I surrender."

Arthur smiled slightly, then stopped exerting force, then turned around to find Jules and asked him to come and tie up the middle-aged bandit.

Perhaps forced by Arthur's momentum, Jules couldn't even think of escaping.

He had moved to the end of the team and had no choice but to dismount and tie people up.

The reason why Arthur didn't kill this man, in addition to the fact that he was a modern soul in the 21st century, King Robert had not died yet, which was a very important factor.

At this time, the order had not collapsed, and even murderers could choose to join the Night's Watch on the Northern Wall to escape the death penalty.

In addition, Arthur also knew that there was an extremely powerful law of cause and effect in the game of power:

People who actively kill people will be killed by the same means, except for blood revenge.

Even POV characters (visual characters) cannot escape this law of cause and effect.

When Ned Stark appeared, he killed the black deserter with a sword. He obeyed the laws of the North. Later, he was killed by a sword in King's Landing, which also obeyed Joffrey's law.

Jon Snow stabbed his own man, Qhorin Halfhand, to death with a sword, and he was also stabbed to death by his own man; Young Wolf Lord Robb was stabbed to death by Old Flayer with a dagger, and Old Flayer was also stabbed to death by his son, Young Flayer, with a dagger; Snow's wildling girlfriend shot many villagers to death, and she was also shot to death by a villager boy with an arrow; The Queen of Thorns of the Rose family poisoned Joffrey to death with poison, and she was also poisoned to death by Jaime...

Even the nameless little people follow this law of cause and effect:

Brieney the Beauty met three Wolf soldiers on the way to escort Jaime to King's Landing. Those three soldiers killed three maids, two of whom died quickly and one died slowly. The three soldiers also died quickly and one died slowly. So in a magical world like Game of Thrones, it is better to keep a low profile and be positive and kind.

After Roger was tied up, Arthur said to the young bandit opposite:

"Do you surrender yourself, or do I surrender for you?"

The young bandit was probably a little naive, and was stunned for a moment before he said, "Why should I surrender? Can't I just run?"

Then he ordered the bandits on foot to turn around and run away.

Brynden's idea was good, but there was just one small problem.

That is, Arthur's infantry had caught up.

The eleven bandits turned around and prepared to flee, and found a group of Bracken soldiers rushing up about thirty or forty steps in front of them.

And behind them stood the man who had chopped Roger down with three swords.

On both sides were dense and irregular beech forests.

The choice was clear.

At least the beech forest would not cut people.

[You will meet the opponent's eleven with a team of fifty people]

Arthur smiled slightly, knowing that the bandits could not run away, so he called the six people around him and strode forward.

The battle went smoothly. By the time dinner was halfway through, the eleven captured bandits had been tied up.

The farmer's daughter and the village chief's wife were also rescued.

Fortunately, the village chief's wife did not become an "overnight wife".

[Two-handed weapon proficiency plus three]

[Task: Find the bandits and help the people recover the stolen property. Completed, experience plus 500, Riverside Village favorability plus three]

Just as Arthur was about to add points, a voice came from the captives:

"How dare you tie me up? Do you know who I am?"
